name: Told by the Heirloom
why_it_works: Telling the story from the object's point of view is unexpected, so people keep watching to see who is talking. It reframes a high price as a cost per generation, and luxury buyers are buying meaning and permanence more than metal.

hook.pattern: The product speaks in first person with a specific lifetime fact.
examples: Three generations have checked the time on me.
I spent 30 years in a drawer. Then this happened.

variables.name: heirloom_item
variables.example: a gold signet ring with a worn crest

variables.name: events_count
variables.description: How many weddings or milestones it has seen

variables.name: first_owner
variables.description: The first owner, described without real names if needed

variables.name: hard_chapter
variables.description: A quiet or hard period in its life, a full spoken sentence in the object's voice, 9 words or fewer
variables.example: When he passed, nobody could bear to wear me

variables.name: new_owner
variables.example: his great-granddaughter, on her wedding day

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What viewers can do next, starting with a capital letter, spoken, 5 words or fewer

variables.name: care_tip
variables.description: One practical care tip for this kind of piece, a full sentence
variables.example: Store it alone in soft cloth and wipe it after every wear.

variables.name: worked_number
variables.description: The price worked out per year of wear, as a real calculation
variables.example: $2,400 over 70 years is about $34 a year

craft.notes: Write every line as the object. Keep it calm, never salesy: an heirloom does not shout. Use one sentence per era. The restoration beat is the only clip, because the hands and the slow turn of the piece show craft better than any still.

do_not: Make the object sound cute or jokey; luxury needs restraint
Show or imitate another luxury house's logo or signature design
Invent a provenance the client cannot back up
